1.explanation: The files 'lighthouse-core/computed/metrics/interactive.js' and 'lighthouse-core/audits/metrics/interactive.js' are key to the bug because they handle the computation and auditing of the 'Time to Interactive' (TTI) metric. The error 'NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD' is directly related to the logic in these files that determines when a page is considered interactive. The issue arises when there is no sufficient CPU idle period after a slow FCP, which these files are responsible for detecting and reporting.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario involves a Lighthouse report showing a 'NO_TTI_CPU_IDLE_PERIOD' error when the page has a slow First Contentful Paint (FCP) but is idle immediately after it. This occurs when using DevTools with provided throttling. The error is visible in the performance metrics section of the Lighthouse report, where 'Time to Interactive' and 'Total Blocking Time' show errors due to the lack of a CPU idle period.
